Now that you mention it that is a damned good question. Hopefully someone knowledgeable answers it.

It would be easier to state what I do not use: Gnome 3, Unity, and tiling environments like i3.

I'm planning on buying or putting together a new machine by June. I will install the KDE Manjaro spin on that machine. It looks gorgeous, it runs great, and it doesn't mangle the interface the way some other DE's have in recent times. If you think Microsoft's design peaked with Windows 7, you will like KDE. Some of the KDE suite of applications are rudundant, but easily removed (going to assume you are not going to build from scratch with something like Arch).

LXQT looks good enough and runs amazing on older hardware. I just put Manjaro LXQT on an old machine with 2GB of RAM and a Celeron processor. It runs smooth as silk for web browsing, playing HD video below blu-ray bitrate qualities, productivity, and communication. This is a machine that was running Windows Vista and was otherwise destined for the scrap heap by a client.

MATE is also very functional, and not a resource hog. How it looks can vary wildly. If you have a distro with lots of tweaking tools built in (like Ghost BSD) it looks great. If you just install it from a repository, you may find it to be bland off the bat. The Ubuntu MATE 16.04 beta has a lot of options available by default, and can be tailored to look very good.

Budgie has some good ideas, and looks very clean. But it doesn't operate all that smoothly when I use it. Perhaps it works better in conjuction with the associated distro (Solus), but my experience has been mixed installing it in Lubuntu, or trying the Manjaro spin. Something about Gnome 3 based desktops are just janky as fuck for me. It also idles at 30% CPU usage for me, which is illogical.

xfce is good, but you can get the same "low overhead" performance with better looking environments. Lumina DE is interesting, but still in the very early stages. Cinnamon is very reliable, if not particularly exciting. The Pantheon environment in Elementary OS is excellent if you plan to use a lot of web apps through Chromium (but you gotta tweak the "macness" out of it in terms of minimize/maximize/close). Peppermint Linux uses a sort of hybrid between LXDE for the panel and XFWM for the window manager. Throw in docky and you have a desktop that looks good, is light on resources, and keeps the familiar "start menu" sctructure).

I guess overall my recommendation is KDE. I never used to like it as much during the Gnome 2 days, but then Gnome 3 happened, Microsoft became obsessed with tiles, and Plasma 4/5 turned into very good looking and functional pieces of work. Plasma 5.5 has been my go to for the past three months, and it has never steered me wrong.
